title: Patchwork dependencies inventory (ad-hoc tracker)
body:
Patchwork Dependencies Inventory — ad-hoc tracker

Context:
Small rapid inventory to capture one-off cross-team dependencies that surfaced during the Feb launch rehearsal. Not intended as canonical system of record — lightweight, intentionally informal. Use to triage quick owners and cover short gaps for weekend coverage and short-lived rollouts.

How to use this sheet (3 bullets):
- Row-per-dependency, assign a single owner (can be temporary) and an expected ETA for mitigation.
- Use the Quick Risk (H/M/L) and Operational Impact (1-5) to sort and allocate labor.
- Add an explicit rollback or mitigation action in the Notes column. If none exists, flag for on-call review.

Columns (current view):
- id | area | dependency | owner | quick_risk | ops_impact | est_lift_hours | blocker_until | status | notes

Sample rows (freeform):
1 | serving-runtime | model-variant routing table missing region fallback entry | Maya Rodriguez | H | 5 | 6 | until routing PR merged | open | temp fallback to smaller quantized model; PR INF-2981 created; needs SRE verification after deploy
2 | console | rollout flag toggle not mirrored to dedicated accounts | Liam O'Connor | M | 4 | 4 | until feature flag propagation OK | in_progress | manual resync run; schedule small canary for 10 tenants tonight
3 | private-deployments | customer KMS policy edge-case for rewrap | Kenji Yamamoto | H | 5 | 12 | until KMS policy patch | blocked | security review needed; SE-owner notified; propose short-lived allowlist for affected tenant
4 | platform-engineering | autoscaler burst config diff between regions -> throttles | Sven Berg | M | 3 | 3 | mitigated | closed | conservative burst increase applied; monitor 24h
5 | observability | missing token-level cost tag for one route | Aisha Patel | L | 2 | 1 | resolved | closed | tagging fix merged to staging; will roll to prod in next deploy

Quick rollup (engineers/PMs):
- Total open items: 3
- Estimated total lift: ~22 hours (sum of est_lift_hours for open/in_progress/blocked)
- Top 2 risks (by ops_impact): model-variant routing (Maya), private KMS edge-case (Kenji)

Immediate asks (this doc):
- Maya: get routing PR to staging and drop a note in #serving-runtime when ready (ETA: 2026-02-18 EOD).
- Kenji: confirm whether allowlist is acceptable temporary mitigation; if not, propose explicit customer communication draft (owner: SE intake).
- Liam: run nightly flag propagation scrub for 48 hours, capture any resync failures as INF tickets and add to this sheet.

Open questions / Known unknowns:
- How many dedicated tenants are affected by the flag propagation gap? Quick query exists but not run (ask Liam to run in the morning).
- Does security accept short-lived allowlist for KMS rewrap while patch is applied? If not, need to schedule an emergency rollback path.

Suggested next steps (priority ordering):
1) Stabilize high-risk items with temporary mitigations (today/tomorrow).
2) Get short postmortem note into Confluence for each closed item (owner adds 1-paragraph).
3) Convert persistent or recurring items into proper Jira backlog tickets with components and owners assigned.

Notes to self (Aisha):
- This is intentionally terse — follow-ups should be tickets, not long Drive edits.
- Keep this doc alive only while the rehearsal/launch window is active; archive after 7 days of no open items.

Changelog (mini):
2026-02-15 initial capture during rehearsal (Aisha)
2026-02-16 added Maya row after routing call; assigned PR INF-2981 (Maya)
2026-02-18 Kenji updated KMS status to blocked; awaiting security input

Slack refs: #serving-runtime, #ops-coverage, #private-deployments
Jira refs: INF-2981, INF-3004 (pending)

-- end of sheet --
